items.title: Chronic stress activates the HPA axis
items.claim: The hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis produces cortisol in response to stress. What does chronic activation cause?

options.text: Sustained elevation of cortisol is associated with immune suppression, abdominal fat deposition, hippocampal atrophy, and increased cardiovascular risk — moving stress from a psychological to a physiological problem
Cortisol stops being produced under chronic stress

items.reveal:
Hans Selye described the General Adaptation Syndrome (alarm, resistance, exhaustion) in 1936. Bruce McEwen's concept of 'allostatic load' (1998) extends this: the wear-and-tear of repeated stress responses contributes to chronic disease.

Whitehall studies (Marmot, 1967 onwards) linked low job control with worse health outcomes via stress pathways. The relationship between psychosocial stress and cardiovascular disease is robust across cohorts but causality is hard to isolate from confounders.
items.why: The mind-body distinction breaks down when looking at chronic stress. Psychological experience produces measurable biological change with health consequences.

items.title: Milgram's obedience rate
items.claim: In Stanley Milgram's 1963 baseline experiment, participants were ordered to deliver what they believed were increasing electric shocks to a stranger. What proportion went all the way to the maximum 450 volts?
items.reveal_title: Around 65% continued to the maximum level
items.reveal:
In Milgram's original Yale study (1963), 26 of 40 participants (65%) continued to the 450V switch under verbal pressure from the experimenter.

Replications, including Burger (2009) in modified form, found broadly similar obedience patterns.
items.why: Situational pressure from a perceived authority figure can override personal moral judgement to a degree most people predict incorrectly.

items.title: The multi-store model was too simple for working memory
items.claim: Atkinson and Shiffrin's 1968 multi-store model split memory into sensory, short-term and long-term stores. What replaced its account of short-term memory?

options.text: Nothing — the multi-store model is unchanged

Baddeley and Hitch's 1974 working memory model — a central executive coordinating a phonological loop, visuospatial sketchpad and (later) episodic buffer — better fitted evidence that STM is not a single unitary store

items.reveal:
Patients with impaired STM (e.g., KF, studied by Shallice and Warrington 1970) could nonetheless retain visual information and form new long-term memories — evidence STM had components. Baddeley and Hitch (1974) proposed a multi-component working memory. The episodic buffer was added by Baddeley in 2000.

The multi-store model is still taught as a stepping stone but is superseded for STM specifically.
items.why: Models that fit the original data often fail later, more specific data. Working memory's multiple components matter for education, clinical assessment and cognitive neuroscience.
